title: Beyond the 956: Regina Torné, beloved Mexican actress of “Como agua para chocolate,” dies at 82
excerpt: Regina Torné, the Mexican actress best remembered as Mamá Elena in Como agua para chocolate and as Tía Gloria in El Chavo del 8, died November 11, 2026, at 82 in Mexico City.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Regina Torné, the Mexican actress best remembered as the stern Mamá Elena in Like Water for Chocolate, has died at 82.

Torné died Wednesday, November 11, 2026, at her home in Mexico City, the National Actors Association (ANDA) regional delegation in Veracruz and the Centro de Teatro y Cultura announced. El Heraldo de México, TV Azteca’s Ventaneando, Excélsior, Univision and Quién also reported her death. No cause of death has been publicly disclosed.

Born Rosa Virgen del Pilar Martina Incháustegui Anaya on July 21, 1944, in Villahermosa, Tabasco, Torné began her career in 1962 as a jazz singer after studying drama. She went on to build a six-decade career across film, television and theatre.

Spanish-speaking audiences first embraced her in 1978 as Gloria — known to viewers as Tía Gloria — in four episodes of El Chavo del 8. Her defining role came in 1992, when she played Mamá Elena in Como agua para chocolate (Like Water for Chocolate), directed by Alfonso Arau and based on Laura Esquivel’s novel. The performance won her the Ariel Award for Best Actress.

Torné was also a familiar face in Mexican telenovelas, where she often played the villain, including Clarisa, Retrato de familia, La chacala, Cielo rojo and La loba.

Rest in Peace, Regina Torné.

Sources: El Heraldo de México; TV Azteca (Ventaneando); Excélsior; Univision; Quién.
